plain.text: A Pharisee named Nicodemus, a leader of the Jews, came to Jesus at night. He said, "Rabbi, we know you are a teacher who has come from God." Jesus answered, "No one can see the kingdom of God unless they are born again," or "born from above". Nicodemus asked how a grown person could be born again. Jesus said, "No one can enter the kingdom of God unless they are born of water and the Spirit." The Spirit is like the wind: you hear it, but you don't know where it comes from or where it is going.

"How can this be?" asked Nicodemus. Jesus said he spoke about what he knew. No one has gone up into heaven except the Son of Man who came from heaven. Just as Moses lifted up the bronze snake in the desert, so the Son of Man must be lifted up, so that everyone who believes in him may have eternal life.

For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son, so that everyone who believes in him will not perish but have eternal life. God did not send his Son to condemn the world, but to save it. Whoever believes in him is not condemned. Light has come into the world, but people loved darkness because their deeds were evil. Whoever lives by the truth comes into the light.

Jesus and his disciples went into the Judean countryside and baptised people. John was also baptising nearby. John's disciples complained that everyone was going to Jesus. John said he was glad, like the friend of a bridegroom. "He must become greater; I must become less."

The one who comes from above is above all. He speaks the words of God, for God gives the Spirit without limit. The Father loves the Son and has put everything in his hands. Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, but whoever rejects the Son will not see life.

summary.bigIdea: God loves the world so much that he gave his Son, so that everyone who believes in him will have eternal life.
points: Jesus tells Nicodemus that people must be born again, of water and the Spirit.
"For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son."
John the Baptist says, "He must become greater; I must become less."
summary.reflection: Nicodemus came to Jesus at night with honest questions. What questions would you bring to him?
